title: Photon-efficient quantum repeater chains via hyperentanglement-assisted purification
authors: Vinay Kumar, Krishan Joshi, Claudio Cicconetti
abstract: Linear quantum repeater chains based on Werner-state purification (the BBPSSW protocol) and entanglement swapping (the BDCZ scheme) are fundamental to entanglement distribution in quantum networks. However, they operate under a stringent operation reliability threshold and rely on resource-intensive recurrence purification rounds, each consuming two entangled pairs to probabilistically produce one. In the literature, hyperentanglement has been proposed to exploit multiple degrees of freedom (DOF), such as polarisation and spatial modes, to encode independent entangled states within a single photon pair. This has led to the definition of DAEPP (DOF-Assisted Entanglement Purification Protocol), which we propose to integrate with the BDCZ scheme, resulting in a chain protocol that we call DAHR (DOF-Assisted Hyperentanglement Repeater). The DAEPP step distils the fidelity of a DOF by consuming other(s). In this work, we propose and analyse a DAHR variant which integrates DAEPP at every segment of an end-to-end path combined with BDCZ. We derive a closed-form end-to-end fidelity recursion that embeds single-segment DAEPP into the BDCZ scheme and give a strict resource lower bound for any BDCZ baseline utilising BBPSSW purification to match DAHR's per-segment effective fidelity. At a representative asymmetric operating point informed by prior experiment, we show numerically that matching DAHR's single-photon-pair performance requires two to three rounds of BBPSSW purification. Additionally, below a critical operation reliability, no amount of BBPSSW rounds matches DAHR's one DAEPP round performance.
summary: This paper introduces the DAHR protocol, a novel quantum repeater chain that enhances entanglement distribution by incorporating hyperentanglement-assisted purification (DAEPP) at every segment. By deriving a new fidelity recursion, the authors prove that DAHR is significantly more resource-efficient than established methods like BBPSSW purification, especially at low operating fidelities.
main_problem: The primary goal is to improve the efficiency of entanglement distribution over long distances in quantum networks by developing a superior quantum repeater chain protocol.
main_result: The proposed DAHR protocol, which integrates hyperentanglement-assisted purification (DAEPP) into the repeater chain, significantly outperforms existing methods, requiring fewer resource pairs to achieve the same fidelity.
method: The authors derive a closed-form, end-to-end fidelity recursion by embedding the DAEPP step into the standard BDCZ entanglement swapping scheme.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a linear chain of N segments, utilizing hyperentangled photon pairs encoding independent states across multiple degrees of freedom (e.g., polarization and spatial modes).
key_observables: End-to-end fidelity ($F^N$), resource consumption (number of entangled pairs consumed per segment).
important_parameters: Operation reliability threshold, initial polar/spatial fidelities ($F_P, F_S$), and the number of purification rounds ($k$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the spatial DOF is the more robust mode ($F_S > F_P$) and uses the general Werner model for purification analysis.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the end-to-end fidelity ($F_N$) versus the number of segments ($N$) for raw BDCZ, BDCZ with $k$ BBPSSW rounds, and the proposed DAHR protocol, showing DAHR's superior performance.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews existing repeater limitations, then derives the DAEPP fidelity, and finally constructs the DAHR protocol by integrating DAEPP into the BDCZ recurrence relation, concluding with a strict resource lower bound comparison.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, theoretically derived improvement to quantum network protocols, directly impacting the feasibility and scaling of quantum communication infrastructure.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The DAHR per-segment workflow. Left to right follows: quantum repeater A, the noisy channel, and quantum repeater B. Hyperentangled pairs are generated by a source in the middle (MidPointSource scheme [3]). The spatial degree of freedom (in red) is consumed to upgrade the polarisation mode before chain-level entanglement swapping.

FIG. 2. End-to-end fidelity FN vs chain length at the operating point (F (0) P , F (0) S ) = (0.85, 0.95), with BDCZ parameters as ηBSA = p1 = p2 = 0.99. (a) ideal purification operation reliability (ηm = pg = 1); (b) matched operation reliability (ηm = pg = 0.99). DAHR (one DAEPP round) stays above BDCZ-with-2-BBPSSW for the ideal purification operation reliability case and is even marginally better than BDCZ-with-3-BBPSSW for the matched operation reliability case across the number of segment N range.

FIG. 3. Raw pairs consumed per segment versus delivered per-segment fidelity for the ideal and matched purification-operation reliability regimes. In the ideal regime, DAHR (one DAEPP, blue, solid circle) achieves (0.926, 1.15), while the BBPSSW staircase (red, solid square, k = 1 . . . 5) requires k = 2–3 rounds to reach comparable performance, corresponding to 5.7–12.8 raw pairs. In the matched-operation reliability regime, DAHR (one DAEPP, blue, hollow diamond) attains (0.915, 1.17), whereas BBPSSW (red, hollow square) must exceed k = 3 rounds to approximately match this point, requiring about 15 raw pairs.

FIG. 4. For Corollary 1 with DAHR and BBPSSW at the same operation reliability x = ηm = pg. (a) Fidelity head-to-head for DAHR’s one DAEPP round F ′(FP , FS; x, x) (blue) and BBPSSW’s ∞-round ceiling F †(x, x) (red). The two cross at ηcrit ≈0.973, and the shaded band 0.967 < x < ηcrit (above the bifurcation ≈0.967) is the window where one DAEPP round beats BBPSSW’s whole iteration. (b) Above ηcrit BBPSSW can match DAHR but at exploding photon cost. Pairs/segment to match diverges as x →η+ crit, against DAHR’s flat ∼1.15 pairs/segment.

FIG. 5. Single-round DAEPP advantage F ′(FP , FS) −F ′(FP , FP ) over the spatial-polarization fidelity plane (ideal operation reliability). The region is Positive (red) wherever FS > FP . The star here marks the represented operating point in the work, that is, (0.85, 0.95). The diagonal FS = FP is the BBPSSW-equivalent line.
